title: feat: nut-18 mint preferences (ms, fr, sm)

body:
# NUT: https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/381

## Summary

Aligns the NUT-18 / NUT-26 mint-preferences fields with cashubtc/nuts#381 (which consolidates and supersedes cashubtc/nuts#380).

- `ms` (`mint_strict`, TLV 0x09) — was already on this branch
- `fr` (`fee_reserve`, TLV 0x0a) — additional fee reserve the payer adds when paying from a mint outside a non-strict mint list
- `sm` (`supported_methods`, TLV 0x0b, repeatable) — payment methods the sending mint must support (e.g. `bolt11`, `bolt12`, `onchain`)

## Motivation

The original branch implemented only `ms` from cashubtc/nuts#380. That proposal has been replaced by cashubtc/nuts#381, which keeps `ms` but adds two companion fields to cover the broader "preferred-mint with extra fee allowance" and "required payment-method capability" cases the spec authors wanted to express together.

## Changes

- `RawPaymentRequest`: add `fr?: number | bigint` and `sm?: string[]`
- `PaymentRequest`: add `feeReserve` (`Amount`) and `supportedMethods` to the class; plumb through `toRawRequest`, `toEncodedCreqA`, `toEncodedCreqB`, `fromRawRequest`, `fromEncodedRequest` (creqB path)
- `DecodedTLVPaymentRequest`: add `feeReserve?: bigint` and `supportedMethods?: string[]`
- TLV codec: add tags 0x0a (`fee_reserve`, u64) and 0x0b (`supported_methods`, string, repeatable); refresh top-level tag table
- Add `get isMintListStrict()` on `PaymentRequest` that resolves the spec's default-to-true semantic — returns `undefined` when no mint list is set, `mintsStrict !== false` otherwise
- Tests: NUT-26 spec test vector for the combined `ms`/`fr`/`sm` payload, creqA + creqB round trips, default-absence behaviour, full `isMintListStrict` matrix

## Reviewer Notes

- Wire identity preserved: all three fields are only serialized when explicitly set, so existing encoded requests round-trip byte-identical
- `mintsStrict` continues to reflect raw wire state (undefined when absent). The spec's "absent means true when `m` is set" semantic is exposed via the `isMintListStrict` getter rather than mutated into the field on decode — keeps roundtrip clean and avoids gaining a tag the original didn't carry
- `feeReserve` uses `Amount` in the class, mirroring how `amount` is handled; raw/TLV layers stay as numeric/bigint
